name: Transcreation Pipeline
description: Automated 5-stage transcreation pipeline (cultural audit, data localization, local GEO, brief, native-language writing, QA) that runs as the FIRST workflow step for files carrying the Transcreation label, ahead of AI Pre-translation. On success it routes straight to Proofreading; on failure or an untranslated result it falls back into the standard pipeline (AI Pre-translation -> TM Pre-translation -> AI Proofreader -> Translation -> Proofreading) so nothing gets stuck.
_comment_authenticationType: workflow-step-type modules require crowdin_agent, not crowdin_app - this is DIFFERENT from the OAuth flow used by the subtitle-timing-app precedent (which is an editor-right-panel app using authentication.type: crowdin_app). NOT YET VERIFIED against a live install - the exact token-exchange mechanics for crowdin_agent are assumed-analogous to crowdin_app in lib/crowdinAuth.js pending a real install test. See README.

workflow-step-type._comment_ports: PLACEHOLDER - confirm exact input port(s) against the real workflow editor once this step is actually inserted. Routing model (per user decision): this step sits FIRST in the chain, ahead of AI Pre-translation. 'translated' output routes directly into Proofreading, skipping the rest of the normal chain entirely. 'fallback' routes into the existing AI Pre-translation step, so a failed/untranslated string still gets a normal shot at translation via AI Pre-translation -> TM Pre-translation -> AI Proofreader -> Translation -> Proofreading, rather than being parked. This replaces the earlier 'skipped = parked' framing - see the plan doc's Locked decisions section.
